sections.strategy: No new strategic announcements this week; the only regulatory filing was a 2 October PDMR notice covering new LTIP awards to executive directors (granted 1 October) and a joint-ownership transfer of vested shares by Third Party Brands Director Jeremy Stakol. The strategy remains the one set out in the 17 September half-year results: international growth (H2 international sales forecast +20.5%) offsetting a softer UK, plus warehouse cost savings and continued growth of Total Platform brands.
sections.pricing: Next's 17 September half-year update cut UK H2 sales growth guidance to 2.0% (from 2.8%), citing rising inflation, higher mortgage costs and a weak jobs market, and warned that tax rises in the 28 October Budget would add to the pressure. Full-year profit guidance was still raised by £12m to £1.255bn, helped by £7m of extra cost savings, mainly in warehousing. Expect a firm line on cost prices and margin protection in AW27 negotiations.
sections.gossip: Next had reportedly drawn up plans for a bid for Harvey Nichols over the summer, but the department store went to Mike Ashley's Frasers Group out of administration in August. The Total Platform acquisition pipeline (most recently Russell & Bromley in January 2026) is therefore still open for the next distressed brand. In the City, consensus is split roughly evenly between Buy and Hold, with targets ranging from about £130 (Citi, neutral) to £180 (Berenberg, buy); the next trading statement is expected around 5 November.
soWhat: Next is guiding UK growth down to 2% while still raising profit through cost savings. Suppliers should expect tougher cost-price conversations for AW27 and prepare value-engineering options (fabric weight, trims, yield) rather than straight price holds.

International sales are forecast to grow 20.5% in H2, so Next's volume growth is increasingly outside the UK. Suppliers with flexible lead times who can support wider size, climate and market ranges for overseas sites are best placed to win incremental volume.

Next missed out on Harvey Nichols, but it is still acquiring distressed brands to move onto Total Platform. Each new brand brings a supply base that NSL may consolidate, which is an opening for suppliers already approved by Next to pitch for the acquired brands' programmes.
